Subject: Re: Clarifying no-train / data-sovereignty evidence for R&D Innovations

Hi Jonas / Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier. Legal followed up with two specific asks before procurement can move to PO: 1) a binding "no-training" commitment for the Hosted API for the scopes we discussed (product telemetry & user-submitted prompts), and 2) documented evidence that subprocessor access and data residency controls are enforced for EU workloads (we need the subprocessor list plus a short process flow that shows how requests for data access / transfers are authorized).

A few specifics from our counsel:
- The no-train clause needs to apply to both model improvement and derivative training for any models used to serve our requests.
- If Redwood uses third-party subprocessors that could access prompt/response data, we need the list and confirmation of contractual protections (and whether those subprocessors are permitted to train on downstream derivatives).
- If any export or cross-border processing is possible, we need the technical and contractual safeguards described.

Can you provide a DPA excerpt with the proposed wording, the current subprocessor roster, and any runbook/evidence you can share? We understand some things can be redacted but need enough detail for our privacy/compliance review.

Thanks — can you aim for a response by Monday so procurement can keep momentum?

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Grant
Senior Counsel, R&D Innovations
olivia@rndinc.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@rndinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying no-train / data-sovereignty evidence for R&D Innovations

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the items you requested and summarizing our approach below to make review faster. We can redline the DPA excerpt into your template if helpful (happy to do that in parallel).

Files attached: redwood_dpa_excerpt-no-train-v2.pdf; subprocessor_list_2027-04.csv; evidence_process_flow.png

Short answers / scope:
- No-training commitment: For Hosted API usage tied to your account and API keys, Redwood will commit contractually to not use prompts/responses for model training or improvement. The DPA excerpt contains the clause we propose (see section 4.2 in the attached PDF). This applies to: production requests, test data submitted via your production tokens, and logged prompt/response pairs.

- Subprocessors: The attached CSV lists subprocessors with locations and processing categories. For any subprocessor with potential access to content, our contractual terms forbid downstream model training on customer content unless the customer provides explicit opt-in. That is reflected in the DPA language and in our standard subprocessor addendum.

- Data residency & transfers: For EU-region workloads we pin processing to EU-hosted clusters by default for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API, we provide region routing and a contractual commitment to process EU-designated data within the EU unless required by law (we notify customers and minimize transfer surface). The evidence_process_flow.png shows the access-control gate, audit log flow, and the process for responding to legal process requests.

Operational notes / caveats:
- Dedicated and Private deployments: we can include the same no-train commitment and technical controls, and we can add stricter contractual language for subprocessor restrictions where you require it.
- Hosted edge cases: short-term diagnostic captures (e.g., to investigate an outage) are possible but are audited, time-limited, and excluded from model training pipelines by default. If you want absolute prohibition even for ephemeral diagnostic captures, we can add explicit language.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Please review the attached DPA excerpt and mark any redlines. We can prepare a full DPA redline on your template.
2) If you want, we can provide the SOC2 traceability artifact under NDA (we've provided this to other enterprise customers).
3) I'll open a DocuSign envelope with the DPA excerpt once we align on wording.

If helpful, Marissa from Sales will coordinate procurement logistics (pricing/po path) and Karthik will be the technical lead for the evidence call.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Clarifying no-train / data-sovereignty evidence for R&D Innovations

Jonas — this is helpful, thank you. We reviewed the excerpt and the subprocessor roster. A few quick clarifications from Legal before we proceed to DocuSign:

1) Please add an explicit sentence in the no-train clause that forbids downstream use "for model improvement, fine-tuning, or derivative training" without customer opt-in. The clause in your PDF already covers training, but Legal wants that expanded language.
2) For subprocessors located outside the EU, can you confirm that contractual protections are identical (i.e., they are bound to the no-train/no-derivative use by contract) and that you will list any future such subprocessors 30 days prior to onboarding?
3) The evidence flowchart is sufficient for our initial review; please supply the SOC2 traceability artifact under NDA as mentioned so our security team can verify controls.

If you can send a redline with the additional sentence and the SOC2 artifact under an NDA link, procurement will prepare the PO and we can sign. We prefer DocuSign for final execution.

Happy to jump on a quick call if easier — Sam is copied for scheduling.

Best,
Olivia
